quality.reason: The report is well-structured with sourced tweets, scores, and engagement metrics, but leaked LLM meta-commentary at the start and equal scoring of a legitimate ETF inflow signal alongside shill-like promotional content indicates filtering/quality-control issues.

Well-structured digest with genuinely actionable fleet health, PnL, and position metrics, but 4 of 5 signals are duplicate BTC entries from the same scanner with near-identical strength (no dedup) and the news section contains a broken '[[]]' link placeholder, indicating partial noise and formatting degradation.

Well-structured review with a clear comparative strategy-health table, trend deltas, and a prioritized SOL CRITICAL flag showing the assigned stochastic strategy underperforming alternatives by ~50 points — a concrete, actionable signal to reassign strategy; only minor deductions for truncated risk-flag detail and no explicit recommended action.

Well-structured output with clear actionable alerts (SOL 97% and TAO 92% ask-weighted orderbooks are genuinely extreme signals), clean data table with relevant metrics, though the 74% ETH alert is borderline threshold noise and content lacks actual whale transaction data despite the job name.

The report body contains genuinely actionable signal (specific health deltas, whale-monitor 0% uptime flagged, source issue identified), but leaked internal meta-text at the start ('Good — news-timeline compacted again... Now deliver the Discord report') is a delivery defect that should have been stripped before posting to Discord.

Well-structured scan header with transparent methodology disclosure (including honest reporting of a rate-limited Semantic Scholar lookup) and verified paper count, but the visible sample is truncated before any actual paper findings or actionable insights can be assessed.

Redundant install pattern: 'brew tap antonriorodr/memo && brew install antonriorodr/memo/memo' — the fully-qualified install form works without a separate tap
No mention of macOS Sequoia+ intermittent Automation permission re-prompts, which can disrupt unattended AppleScript-based CLIs
No minimum macOS version documented; permission flows (System Settings > Privacy > Automation) differ across macOS releases
references/apple-notes.md and references/apple-reminders.md presence is asserted but not verifiable from the excerpt
Positive note: doc self-reports a recent verification stamp and accurately flags which tools are NOT installed — good freshness hygiene, hence 'current' rather than 'stale'

Claim 'Claude was trained on both' (element indices and coordinates) is unverified and likely overstated: Anthropic's computer-use training is screenshot/coordinate-based, so implying index-clicking reliability comes from training is misleading
No dead links or deprecated tools found in excerpt: pyautogui comparison, AX roles (AXButton/AXTextField/AXLink), SOM overlays, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints are all current patterns
Content truncated mid-action-table at 'right_clic' — remaining actions (drag, type, scroll, key events, wait) cannot be reviewed for deprecated patterns
No last-verified date, macOS version requirement, or tool version pinned; makes future staleness hard to audit
Model references ('Claude, GPT, Gemini') are unversioned; naming minimum model generations would prevent silent drift as models deprecate
capture_after parameter and element-index mode are custom/internal conventions with no external spec to check against; correctness cannot be independently verified
Only the first 2000 chars of body were reviewed; the remainder is unverified for dead links or deprecated tooling
Existence of the 5 references/ files is self-reported ('verified present') but cannot be confirmed from this excerpt
No external URLs appear in the visible portion, so link rot cannot be assessed in either direction

No URLs present in the visible body, so dead-link check is inconclusive for the full document; the references/*.md files and hermes-agent skill are not included in this excerpt and cannot be verified

Fast-moving ecosystem risk: CLI flags and subcommands (e.g., Claude Code print mode -p, Codex exec/non-interactive modes, OpenCode TUI options) change frequently and may have drifted since the reference files were written — spot-check against current vendor docs

Minor clarity risk: 'Codex' name collides with OpenAI's deprecated 2021-2023 Codex model API; the reference correctly disambiguates via the @openai/codex npm package, but keep that qualifier to avoid confusion
OpenCode branding has multiple similarly-named projects in the ecosystem; consider pinning the repo/URL (e.g., opencode.ai) in the reference file to prevent ambiguity

The tool called 'cua-driver' does not match the actual trycua/cua project, which ships packages/CLIs named cua, cua-computer, cua-browser, etc.; no 'cua-driver' binary with a 'skills install' subcommand is publicly verifiable, so the command 'cua-driver skills install' and the path '~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver' are likely broken or invented
The GitHub link (github.com/trycua/cua) is live, but it points to the parent project rather than anything named cua-driver, so users following the doc verbatim will hit a dead end at the install step

The doc self-admits the integration is provisional: Hermes autodetection is only a 'planned cua-driver follow-up' and requires manually symlinking a skills directory — fragile instructions that are likely to be superseded or already wrong

'Hermes' is referenced without version, vendor, or context; whether it refers to an internal agent harness or a model family, it is unverifiable from public documentation and may be project-internal jargon that has since been renamed

The claim 'There is no Anthropic-native schema to learn' dismisses Anthropic's official computer-use tool schema (e.g., computer_20250124), which remains the supported path for Claude models via the API; this framing may mislead integrators
No dates, versions, or changelog references anywhere in the excerpt, making it impossible to validate the action vocabulary (capture/som, element-index clicking) against any current API contract
Minor: the training-claim about Claude ('Claude was trained on both') is an unverifiable assertion and may age poorly as models change

Core concept is evergreen and sound: git merge/rebase conflict arbitration, neutral third-party adjudication, and regenerating lockfiles instead of hand-merging are all current best practices — no deprecated git patterns found.

References internal/unverifiable tooling throughout: 'hermes kanban show <task-id>', 'delegate_task', and 'kanban_create(title=..., assignee=..., parents=[...])' cannot be validated against any public tool registry. If the org's orchestration stack has evolved, these are silent breakage points — verify each still exists with these exact names and signatures.
'delegate_task' may not match the current canonical subagent-spawning tool name in the target harness (e.g., Claude Code exposes 'Task', not 'delegate_task'). Confirm the current tool identifier.

The kanban-native flow hardcodes a specific API signature including the 'parents' kwarg; hardcoded tool signatures rot faster than prose. Consider pointing to the live tool schema or a tool-lookup reference instead.
Phrasing "(`terminal` running `hermes kanban show <task-id>`)" is ambiguous — the backticked 'terminal' appears to reference a specific UI surface that may have been renamed; clarify or drop.
